title: The Sum of the XOR of Every Subset

concept.title: Carry a running value down the recursion
body: The **XOR** of a subset combines its numbers bit by bit: a bit of the result is 1 when an odd number of the numbers has that bit set. To add up the XOR values of all `2^n` subsets, decide every number as "in" or "out" while carrying the **XOR of the numbers taken so far** as an argument of the recursion.

No list of chosen numbers is needed, and nothing has to be undone afterwards: the value `current ^ a[i]` exists only inside the second call. When the choices can be summarised in one number, **passing it by value** is simpler than a table that you must restore.

statement: Given `n` non-negative integers, consider all `2^n` subsets of positions (including the empty subset, whose XOR is 0). Print the sum of the XOR of the numbers of each subset.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` integers.

examples.note: The XOR values of the eight subsets are 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 0, with the sum 12.

hints: For every number the recursion has two calls: leave it, or take it.
Pass the XOR of the taken numbers as an argument.
At the end of the numbers return that XOR; the sum of both calls is the answer.

starter.python:
n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: `total(i, current)` returns the sum over all ways to decide the numbers from position `i` on, given the XOR `current` of the numbers already taken. At the end of the list the XOR itself is the value of one subset.
